content: The North Hampshire Hospital, previously known as Basingstoke District Hospital, is a 400-bed facility under the National Health Service (NHS) located in Basingstoke, Hampshire, England. It operates as part of the Basingstoke and North Hampshire NHS Foundation Trust, employing approximately 3,000 staff members and providing care to 180,000 patients annually as of 2006. In 1999, this hospital became the first in Europe to perform surgical procedures using equipment controlled by voice commands. In 2002, it inaugurated a new Postgraduate Medical Centre, known as The Ark Centre. This centre is an independent charity situated on the hospital campus and is managed by the North Hampshire Medical Education Trust, a registered charity. The Ark Centre collaborates with the hospital to deliver a variety of postgraduate educational programs and also functions as an independent conference centre. The Ark Centre partners with organizations such as the Pelican Cancer Foundation, a charity focused on advancing the treatment of pelvic and liver cancers through precision surgical techniques, and the nurse training facility of Southampton University. The Ark Centre specializes in hosting high-tech conferences, including medical and surgical meetings, and is equipped with advanced IT systems and interactive live case presentation capabilities. The charity associated with The Ark also supports a wide range of community activities, including educational and self-help meetings held within the centre itself. Additionally, the hospital has served as a filming location for both series of the Channel 4 comedy Green Wing. In the hospital’s Hunters Courtyard, there is an elephant-shaped fountain designed by sculptor Sioban Coppinger, which was created as part of a children’s play area. The hospital also operates its own radio station, Hospital Radio Basingstoke, which broadcasts on 945 kHz AM and is accessible on channel 6 through the bedside PatientLine units.
